questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to study translation between french and danish. And to speak more french in general.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There were meetings with the mobility-department and the university has a housing-department that was easy to find and where I could go and get my key for the housing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The mobility department distributed a lot of information via e-mail and at information meetings. The teachers from my department helped me choose my courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student residences at different locations in the town. I stayed in a single-room with a private bathroom and shared kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a kitchen that I shared with the rest of the residents on my floor. Unfortunately it wasn't very well-equipped or clean. I had a refrigerator in my room which meant that I didn't need to use the kitchen that much. There was also a dining hall in my building that serves lunch on weekdays.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The residence I lived in (Cité Pierre Houzeau de Lehaie), has two student bars in the basement that are used by student clubs/fraternities. They have rather loud parties, especially in the beginning of the schoolyear.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In my residence there was an issue with the fire-alarm, that went off almost every morning at around 7am due to someone smoking inside the building. The issue went on for several months and was a big problem... aside from all the problems, the housing was very affordable, easy to apply for and located close to the city-centre.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is quite simple to register for courses - the whole process of completing learning agreements and getting them signed takes some time, but I had a lot of help from the erasmus coordinator at Umons and from my teachers.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mobility-department hosted information meetings about the process of getting the learning agreement completed. This was very helpful. The teachers in my department looked at my LA and helped me choose the right courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask your teachers and coordinators for help. And ask your fellow students what courses they like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses in translation from french into danish on MA-level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is much more practical, with more physical class-time and less homework.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the translation courses. FLE was not very relevant and took up a lot of time. The terminologi course has interesting elements but is not very relevant to students from Copenhagen.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Regular groceries were slightly less expensive than I expected. Beer is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't participate in that many activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know that there are very cheap athletic activities at uni. Each department/faculty has a student-organization that hosts parties/activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the parties hosted by the student organizations. I know that there is also a organisation for exchange-students that hosts activities, which seemed like a good opportunity to meet people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is relatively easy and cheap to get to other belgian cities or Paris. Mons is also a lovely town, with lots of bars and thrift stores. There are also museums that are free to visit on the first sunday of each month.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the parties hosted by the student-organizations. Maybe make an effort to find their instagram accounts or similar to know if something is happening.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students in Mons typically leave to go home on the weekends - this means that they usually party/go out on thursdays, and that the town can seem a bit empty over the weekend, so it's nice to go on trips on saturdays or sundays.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Belgians seem very open, talkative and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about the whole registration process. Belgians tend to worry less about deadlines than danish people do, and the teachers and coordinators are hugely helpful if you ask them. If you take translation classes, speak all the french you can there! This of course goes for other situations as well, but the classes really are a great opportunity to practice and to discuss translations with your teachers and fellow students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to speak french regularly.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The issues with the residence where I lives.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
